outcome_definitions_and_analysis_sets.verbatim: The primary outcome was sensitivity of the quantitative FIT for detecting advanced neoplasms at 2 predefined cutoffs: 17-μg Hb/g feces... and 10.2-μg Hb/g feces... in fecal samples scheduled 2 days after intake of aspirin or placebo.
outcome_definitions_and_analysis_sets.analysis: Main analysis: intention-to-screen, samples scheduled for day 2. Prespecified per-protocol analysis: samples collected exactly on day 2.

outcome_definitions_and_analysis_sets.location: PDF p2, Trial Design and Trial Population section
outcome_definitions_and_analysis_sets.verbatim: Advanced neoplasms were defined as the presence of either CRC or advanced adenoma that either was 1 cm or larger in size, had tubulovillous or villous components, or high-grade dysplasia.

reported_secondary_outcomes: specificity, PPV, and NPV of the quantitative test
potential gain in sensitivity by combining results from multiple samples scheduled on days 2-4
sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV of the qualitative test
sex-specific sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV of both tests
outcome_definitions_and_analysis_sets.verbatim_qualification: Further secondary outcomes not reported in this article were likelihood ratios and area under the curve.

outcome_definitions_and_analysis_sets.verbatim: Statistical significance was defined by a 2-sided P value <.05. No adjustments were made for multiple testing. Analyses of secondary outcomes should therefore be regarded as exploratory.
outcome_definitions_and_analysis_sets.CI_method: Wald-adjusted confidence intervals for sensitivity and specificity (Agresti-Coull adjustment) and differences (Agresti-Caffo adjustment).

additional_secondary_claims.location: PDF p4, Secondary End Points section
additional_secondary_claims.verbatim: Compared with results for day-2 samples only, higher sensitivities and lower specificities were observed in both the intervention group and the control group, with little change in the differences in sensitivity between the intervention and control groups.
additional_secondary_claims.referenced_result_location: eTable 3 in Supplement 3; not numerically reproduced in the main article.

additional_secondary_claims.location: PDF p4, Secondary End Points section
additional_secondary_claims.verbatim: Overall, no significant differences were seen, neither in intention-to-screen nor in per-protocol analysis.
additional_secondary_claims.outcome: PPVs and NPVs; Table 3 and eTable 5 in Supplement 3
effect of study site / random intercept
additional_secondary_claims.verbatim: The likelihood ratio test for the null hypothesis of zero variance of the random intercept never achieved statistical significance (P values 0.16 to 0.50), therefore the model without random intercept was retained.

additional_secondary_claims.aspirin: 11 adverse events in 7 participants; 2 serious adverse events in 2 participants (acute appendicitis and acute suppurative cholangitis accompanied by acute kidney injury), requiring hospitalization, considered not related to trial drug.
additional_secondary_claims.placebo: 5 participants reported 6 adverse events; serious adverse events were not reported.

sex_interaction_claim.location: PDF p4, Secondary End Points section
sex_interaction_claim.verbatim: P values for interaction effects between sex and intervention were all statistically nonsignificant and ranged from .08 to .49.

per_protocol_men_claim.location: PDF p4, Secondary End Points section
per_protocol_men_claim.analysis: fecal samples collected exactly 2 days after tablet intake
per_protocol_men_claim.verbatim: Compared with intention-to-screen analysis, differences in sensitivity between the intervention and control group were of greater magnitude among men, with sensitivities that were 23.2 (95% CI, 5.0 to 39.5) and 22.5 (95% CI, 4.5 to 38.6) percentage points higher in the intervention group at the lower cutoff of the quantitative test and for the qualitative test, respectively.
per_protocol_men_claim.additional_claim: Differences in specificity between the intervention and control groups were similar for the per-protocol and intention-to-screen analyses.

reported_overall_conclusion.location: PDF p1, Abstract Conclusions and Relevance; PDF p6, Conclusions section
reported_overall_conclusion.verbatim: Among adults aged 40 to 80 years not using aspirin or other antithrombotic medications, administration of a single dose of oral aspirin prior to fecal immunochemical testing, compared with placebo, did not significantly increase test sensitivity for detecting advanced colorectal neoplasms at 2 predefined cutoffs of a quantitative fecal immunochemical test.
